_comment: Operator-authored directory for the composed V2 server.
STRUCTURE is proven (session log T17, 2026-08-02): entries of stride 0x260, each
owning records of stride 0x134. Every field maps to an exact offset and every
bound is enforced.
ENTRY fields are carried by 0x6503 (session log T31, corpus 001c70b0):
host        <= 0x3e  the CONNECT TARGET. Lands at entry +0x00. On selection the
client parses it as a dotted quad and otherwise resolves it
by DNS (T30 runtime, T31 disassembly). A literal IP bypasses
DNS entirely, which is why the rig uses one.
name        <= 0x0f  display name
raw8        exactly 8 bytes, MEANING UNKNOWN - keep zero
description <= 0xff  display description
At most 16 entries; a 0x6503 declaring 0 entries is a terminal client error.
TWO ENTRIES IS THE MINIMUM FOR A USABLE SERVER SELECT. FUN_00606fc0 substate 1
AUTO-SELECTS entry 1 and resolves immediately when the entry count is 0 or 1; the
interactive list is drawn only at count >= 2 (SERVER-SELECT-SPEC-2026-08-05.md
C.1/D.3). With one entry the player never chooses anything, and a host that fails
to resolve takes the harder screen-state-5 error path instead of the dialog.
Every entry needs at least one record: 0x6502 mode 0 skips a recordless entry, and
FUN_005c7bd0 dereferences entry+0x160 unconditionally when it fills the UI row.
RECORD bounds: unknownField0/unknownField1 <= 15, unknownRaw8 exactly 8,
unknownField2 <= 255, at most 64 records per entry. unknownField0 is the key the
client echoes in its 0x6510 request, so it must be unique within an entry.
Strings are latin1; use { "hex": "..." } for raw bytes.
unknownWord1 is MAXIMUM PLAYERS (record +0x12a); unknownWord6510 is CURRENT
PLAYERS (record +0x12c). Corpus 005c7bd0 fills the UI from cur(+0x12c)/max(+0x12a).
MAXIMUM PLAYERS IS A LIVE GATE, NOT A LABEL: FUN_005bc990 sums the per-area player
counts and refuses the lobby with "Server full. You cannot participate." when that
sum reaches FUN_005c5060 = the SELECTED entry's FIRST record's +0x12a. So 0 is a
permanently full server, and a small number turns real players away.
The 256 below is not a fixture value: it is PAL_V2_MAXIMUM_PLAYERS, which defaults
to the server's own lobby-connection ceiling because a player occupies exactly one
connection. Startup REFUSES any entry pointing at this server whose records
disagree with it (application.js assertDirectoryCapacityIsConfigured), so this
number cannot drift back into being a leftover. It replaced 4, which came from V1's
trace (session6_trace.log:91) and would have refused the lobby at four players.
The client holds only 64 records resident across all entries at once; a larger
directory is legal and is walked in windows.
provenance MUST be "operator" for the production server to start.
TWO ENTRIES, BOTH POINTING AT THE SAME RIG SERVER. The count matters:
FUN_00606fc0 substate 1 AUTO-SELECTS entry 1 when the count is 0 or 1, so the
interactive list is only drawn at count >= 2 and the player can never actually
choose. Both hosts are 192.0.2.121 on purpose - the rig runs ONE server, and an
entry advertising a host with nothing behind it would fail to connect if selected,
which would look like a protocol fault rather than a fixture choice. In production
these are distinct machines.
rigFixture DECLARES THIS FILE AS THE DEVELOPMENT RIG'S. It exempts the file from
the rig-fixture gate, which otherwise refuses private/loopback hosts, placeholder
strings, a zero player cap and non-zero undecoded flag bytes. A PRODUCTION file
omits it and must then pass that gate. See docs/PROTOCOL-VALUE-INVENTORY.md:
every value marked RIG there must be replaced before going live.
(A paragraph here used to say entry-1's host was a second address on the rig LAN,
and that two entries sharing a host would make the choice meaningless. Commit
746b43cd pointed both entries at 192.0.2.121 and explained why above; the old
text was left behind and contradicted the data below. It is corrected rather than
silently dropped: what makes the list interactive is the entry COUNT, and a second
host with nothing behind it would fail to connect when selected - which on a rig
run reads as a protocol fault rather than a fixture choice.)

entries.name: PAL V2 RIG 2
entries.description: Second rig target - the list is only selectable with two entries
